Treat any single number as approximate.

text.p_yest: The high of 39°F was typical for November 13. The normal high for the date is 48°F, and the record is 75°F (1879). The low of 30°F was typical for November 13.
text.t_rec: Lansing has nearly stopped setting record lows
text.p_rec: If Lansing's climate weren't changing, every year would have the same chance of holding a daily record. Since 2000, Lansing has set 11 standing record lows, far fewer than the 61 that chance alone would give, and 68 record highs, close to the 61 that chance alone would give. The 1890s hold the most record highs of any decade (46). Lansing's all-time high is 103°F, on July 6, 2012.
text.t_chg: Lansing's days and nights both warmed. Nights warmed faster.
text.p_chg: Across 157 complete years: Lansing's average low has risen +0.36°F per decade (95% range +0.29 to +0.42), about +5.7°F since 1864. Lansing's average high has risen +0.12°F per decade (95% range +0.06 to +0.17), about +1.9°F since 1864.
text.t_mon: Lows rose in all 12 months. Highs rose in 5 of 12 months.
text.t_rain: Rain and snow: no clear long-term change
text.p_rain: Lansing's yearly precipitation shows no clear long-term change (+0.16 inches per decade, a range that includes zero). The 1991–2020 normal is 33.3 inches a year. The wettest year was 1883 (48.41 in); the driest, 1930 (18.50 in).
